top.title: Steph Curry shooting left-handed? Warriors' Brandin Podziemski made it happen to improve his game
top.description: Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski reacts after a three-point basket against the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of an NBA Cup basketball game, Saturday, Oct. 30, 2026, in San Francisco. (Justine Willard/Associated Press) As Brandin Podziemski huddled with his personal trainer this past summer, exploring how to raise his game, they hit on some ideas. They watched video of New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson, freshly crowned NBA champion. They examined the 3-point shooting volume of players such as Payton Pritchard and Tyler Herro. At some point, Podziemski posed a simple if heavy question: What about Steph? Stephen Curry counts as a model of efficient movement and basketball creativity. And the trainer, Dustin VanLieu, knew exactly how to help Podziemski gain deeper insight from his decorated Golden State Warriors teammate – magically make Curry left-handed. VanLieu flipped videos of Curry – let's pause here for a nod to the power of digital editing tools – to turn No. 30 into a mirrored version of himself. That allowed Podziemski, who is lefty, to study the footwork, ball-handling and shot creation of a left-handed Steph Curry. The images are striking, as Curry scurries around the court like a familiar if semi-fictional character. He dribbles around bewildered opponents, as usual – even dropping Luka Doncic to the hardwood, on what looks like the opposite end of the court than the real-life moment Oct. 30 – but the sight of Curry launching long-range shots with his left hand is strangely captivating. Curry wasn't aware of Podziemski's uncommon preparation until the Chronicle showed him a video after Saturday night's overtime victory over Orlando. Curry intently watched the lefty version of himself for a few moments, then said simply, "That's crazy!" He also acknowledged the logic behind the idea. "Very creative and clever," Curry said. "It makes a lot of sense to see footwork the way he moves, to create space in a way that makes sense to him. That's pretty cool." This was not the only tool Podziemski used in the offseason, merely the most novel. The early returns suggest his work is paying dividends: He's averaging 16.3 points and 4.2 assists, while shooting better than 40% on 6.9 attempts per game from long distance – all surpassing his career highs – entering Wednesday night's road trip opener in Houston. It's just 11 games into the season, but Podziemski clearly is building on the gains he made in last season's final two-plus months, when Curry was sidelined by a knee injury. Now, with Curry back and playing at his customary elite level and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg providing fresh life, the Warriors find themselves rolling along, with eight consecutive wins. Podziemski, still just 23 years old and nearly five months younger than Lendeborg, has become a central piece of the puzzle. top.title: Canada to fast-track permanent residence for 200,000 foreigners in 2027
top.description: The Canada government has announced plans to accelerate permanent residence (PR) processing for up to 200,000 foreign nationals already living in the country in 2027, as part of efforts to reduce immigration application backlogs and provide greater certainty for newcomers. The initiative, announced by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) under the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, will provide additional admissions spaces for selected workers and humanitarian applicants seeking to transition to permanent residence. According to the government, the measure will be implemented through two major groups: a workers’ cohort and a humanitarian cohort, with up to 100,000 spaces allocated to each. The workers’ category will cover eligible foreign workers already living in Canada, alongside their accompanying family members. The government intends to work with provincial and territorial authorities to identify workers who meet regional labour market requirements. Eligible workers will include those who qualify for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), as well as applicants awaiting decisions under selected federal immigration programmes. These programmes include the Atlantic Immigration Program, Start-Up Visa Program, Self-Employed Persons Program, Agri-Food Pilot and Home Care Worker programmes. The humanitarian category, also allocated up to 100,000 spaces, will cover people already in Canada who have been waiting for permanent residence decisions, including applicants under specific family reunification and humanitarian pathways. Among those expected to benefit from the humanitarian allocation are: Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children: Family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have already applied for permanent residence and are awaiting final decisions. Hong Kong residents: Applicants under Canada’s permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, which closed to new applications on August 31, 2026. Ukrainian nationals: Applicants under the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway, which closed to new applications on October 22, 2024. Humanitarian and compassionate applicants: Individuals already in Canada whose applications for permanent residence have received approval in principle. The government said the additional spaces would help it process all remaining applications under the Hong Kong and Ukraine pathways, while also supporting family reunification and fulfilling existing humanitarian commitments. IRCC also said the initiative would help reduce waiting periods for spouses and partners of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with the aim of bringing processing times closer to 12 months for applicants destined for provinces outside Quebec. The department clarified that eligible applicants do not need to submit a separate application or take additional steps to be considered under the temporary initiative. top.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
top.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. top.title: David Warner starts fresh Sandpapergate row after Graeme Hick rejects Khawaja's dressing-room claims
top.description: The infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight following fresh revelations by Usman Khawaja, triggering a war of words between former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick and David Warner. While Hick has strongly rejected Khawaja's claims that the entire Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper, Warner has hit back at the former coach, questioning his appointment and bringing Michael Di Venuto into the debate. What did Graeme Hick say about Khawaja's claims? Hick, who was part of Australia's coaching staff during the 2018 South Africa tour, described Khawaja's allegations as "absolutely false". He maintained that he had no knowledge of any discussions about using sandpaper and only became aware of the incident after seeing the footage on the big screen in Cape Town. Khawaja had claimed that the entire dressing room was aware of the ball-tampering, suggesting that responsibility for the incident went beyond the three players who were eventually punished. Warner responded by taking aim at Hick's appointment as Australia's batting coach, bringing former assistant coach Michael Di Venuto into the discussion. In response to an X post on the interview, Warner wrote: "Let's get the facts straight. Graeme Hick was only appointed because Cricket Australia was unwilling to pay Michael Di Venuto what he deserved. As players, we valued Michael so highly that we even offered to contribute from our own salaries to retain him. These discussions were taking place during the New Zealand tour. That alone speaks volumes about how highly we regarded him and how determined we were to keep him involved. Adds to why Graeme has spoken!!" — davidwarner31 (@davidwarner31) Why has the 2018 Sandpapergate controversy resurfaced? The latest exchange follows the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr, in which the Australia batter revisited the events of the 2018 South Africa tour. His account has reopened questions about how much the dressing room knew about the ball-tampering incident and whether the original investigation captured the full extent of what happened. The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball using a piece of sandpaper. The incident became known as Sandpapergate and led to major sanctions against the players involved. Warner and then Australia captain Steve Smith were handed one-year suspensions by Cricket Australia, while Bancroft received a nine-month ban. The episode also led to widespread criticism of Australian cricket and prompted questions about the team's culture and leadership.

top.title: 2027 Masters: Austin Smotherman still fighting for Augusta invite despite back-to-back fall wins
top.description: What a year 2026 has been for Austin Smotherman. He welcomed his third daughter into the world after contending at the Cognizant Classic earlier in the year . He made his first major championship start at Aronimink a few months later. Not discouraged from the missed cut at the PGA Championship, the 32-year-old Smotherman won for the first time in his 100th start on Tour at the Bank of Utah Championship. He didn't let the time between career win No. 1 and No. 2 last very long. Three weeks later in Bermuda, Smotherman stood in the winner’s circle again after ousting Seamus Power in a two-man playoff after weather cut the tournament short to 54 holes. With all that, his playing status secured through 2029. And now, one more mountain to climb: Finish inside the top 50 of the Official World Golf Ranking. If he clinches that before the end of the season, the No. 51-ranked Smotherman will get his first-ever invite to Augusta National. There's some risk involved — two missed cuts could theoretically send him down, outside the top 60 in the FedExCup fall points and lose his spot in the first two signature events of 2027. It's a bet Smotherman is willing to take considering the possible reward. "Do our best to put up good weeks and earn some more World Ranking points and cap off the fall hopefully on a high note," he said at his press conference at this week’s Austin Championship when asked about his plan for the next couple of weeks. "Can't take away what we did," Smotherman added. "If we miss two cuts coming up, still doing a lot well and it was the best decision I think to go give it a run. The world ranking points system, I don't understand it perfectly, that's for my team to tell me what's going on. I'm just going to go play golf." Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets were not buyers at the NFL trade deadline this year. New York was active, but only to ship off Andre Cisco to Detroit . The Jets do not look like a playoff team this year, but should they have tried harder to add talent at the trade deadline? Jets head coach Aaron Glenn explained why the team did not make any moves at the deadline this year. “Listen, we’re not going to hide from the fact that we’re 2-7. We own that, but, man, we’re still working our asses off to make sure we fix that. We feel like we like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that,” Glenn said on Wednesday, per ESPN’s Rich Cimini. Even if the Jets are playing their opponents closely, they’re still losing games. It is certainly fair to point out that the Jets are still a long way from being a contender. But that could all change during the 2027 offseason. The Jets will have three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. If everything breaks their way, New York could even have three picks in the top 10. Not only could they find a franchise quarterback, but they could also add a few blue-chip players as well. The future is bright for the Jets, but it is still frustrating to see them take a passive approach to the trade deadline. Regardless, next up for New York is a Week 10 home game against Buffalo. top.title: Why USC's perfectionism might be their greatest asset––and liability
top.description: USC players celebrate a made basket during a Big Ten college basketball game against the College of Charleston, Tuesday, November 10, 2026 in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES –– Perfection is cruel, and Sitaya Fagan is learning the harsh reality of excellence. Fagan checked out of the game with minutes left in the fourth quarter, plopped into her chair, and cried. USC led 101-44. 57 points. The USC Trojans defeated the Charleston Cougars 105-44, but the story rests in the palms that held the face of the woman who went 0-for-7. The boulder-sized lump sat in her throat and chest, heavy and immovable, refusing to accept the scoreboard's narrative. Perfection is the culmination of habits amalgamated when nobody's watching. Intensity. Focus. Dedication. Efficiency. This is what USC is building. Jazzy Davidson found Fagan first, wrapped an arm around her and whispered in her ear. I've been there," Davidson said later. "We expect greatness out of all of us and being a perfectionist—it makes her who she is, but there's also a downside to that." The downside. The stone. The tears after a blowout. If you want to understand this USC team, start there. Start with a kid from Australia, miles away from the comforts of home, family and friends, crying over missed shots in a game her team led by 35 at halftime. Start with the feeling that her nine rebounds, three blocks, and two steals meant nothing because the ball wouldn't go through the net. That's not weakness. That's the obverse of the same coin that has Davidson shooting 75% on the season. It's fanatical. It's almost grandiloquent in its devotion. It's the kind of maniacal obsession that either makes championships or breaks them. In Greek mythology, three sisters controlled the threads of life. Clotho spun it. Lachesis measured it. nigeria.title: Canada to fast-track permanent residence for 200,000 foreigners in 2027
nigeria.description: The Canada government has announced plans to accelerate permanent residence (PR) processing for up to 200,000 foreign nationals already living in the country in 2027, as part of efforts to reduce immigration application backlogs and provide greater certainty for newcomers. The initiative, announced by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) under the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, will provide additional admissions spaces for selected workers and humanitarian applicants seeking to transition to permanent residence. According to the government, the measure will be implemented through two major groups: a workers’ cohort and a humanitarian cohort, with up to 100,000 spaces allocated to each. The workers’ category will cover eligible foreign workers already living in Canada, alongside their accompanying family members. The government intends to work with provincial and territorial authorities to identify workers who meet regional labour market requirements. Eligible workers will include those who qualify for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), as well as applicants awaiting decisions under selected federal immigration programmes. These programmes include the Atlantic Immigration Program, Start-Up Visa Program, Self-Employed Persons Program, Agri-Food Pilot and Home Care Worker programmes. The humanitarian category, also allocated up to 100,000 spaces, will cover people already in Canada who have been waiting for permanent residence decisions, including applicants under specific family reunification and humanitarian pathways. Among those expected to benefit from the humanitarian allocation are: Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children: Family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have already applied for permanent residence and are awaiting final decisions. Hong Kong residents: Applicants under Canada’s permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, which closed to new applications on August 31, 2026. Ukrainian nationals: Applicants under the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway, which closed to new applications on October 22, 2024. Humanitarian and compassionate applicants: Individuals already in Canada whose applications for permanent residence have received approval in principle. The government said the additional spaces would help it process all remaining applications under the Hong Kong and Ukraine pathways, while also supporting family reunification and fulfilling existing humanitarian commitments. IRCC also said the initiative would help reduce waiting periods for spouses and partners of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with the aim of bringing processing times closer to 12 months for applicants destined for provinces outside Quebec. nigeria.title: US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears
nigeria.description: The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 soccer World Cup in Qatar due to concerns about security in the Middle East, US media reported Wednesday. Players were informed of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to begin on November 19, US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources. US Soccer, the sport’s governing body in the United States, did not immediately confirm the news or respond to AFP’s request for comment. The war in the Middle East began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran. Multiple sporting events in the Middle East have been affected, including the tennis WTA Finals which were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia — which neighbors Qatar — but are instead now taking place at Indian Wells in the US. This season’s Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia. Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by the Houthis in Yemen. The US is one of 48 teams scheduled to play in the Under-17 World Cup, in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. The Under-17 World Cup shifted to an annual event last year, and is being held in Qatar for five consecutive years. Announcing its host decision in 2024, FIFA said the decision to choose a single host nation for multiple editions centered on the ability to make “use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability”. nigeria.title: Five factors vehicle buyers should consider – Understanding the true cost of ownership in Nigeria
nigeria.description: By Theodore opara Buying a vehicle is a major financial decision, but many Nigerian motorists focus almost entirely on the amount required to acquire one. While the purchase price is an important consideration, it does not tell the complete story of what it takes to own and maintain a vehicle over the years. From routine servicing and parts replacement, to insurance, fuel and unexpected repairs, vehicle ownership comes with recurring expenses that can significantly influence its overall value. For individuals, families and businesses, understanding these costs before making a purchase can help prevent financial surprises and support better decisions. The ownership cost equation Two vehicles with similar showroom prices may have significantly different maintenance requirements and operating costs. One may benefit from an established after-sales network, readily available spare parts and predictable servicing expenses. Another may present challenges when replacement components are required or technical support is unavailable. These differences can influence the overall cost of ownership. For instance, a vehicle that requires expensive repairs or spends considerable time in a workshop may eventually cost its owner more than initially anticipated. For businesses operating fleets, the consequences can be even greater. Every day a vehicle remains unavailable could affect deliveries, customer service, employee movement and revenue generation. Consequently, vehicle buyers should consider not only acquisition costs but also the financial implications of keeping their vehicles operational. Five factors buyers should consider A proper assessment of vehicle ownership costs should include five major areas. First is the purchase price and any associated financing charges. Second is routine maintenance, including scheduled servicing, lubricants, filters, tyres and other consumables. Third is warranty protection, particularly its duration, coverage and exclusions. Fourth is the availability and cost of replacement parts, including access to qualified technicians. Fifth is downtime, which may create additional transportation expenses, lost business opportunities and reduced productivity. Although some expenses are difficult to forecast, obtaining reliable information before purchasing can help buyers make more informed comparisons. They also need dependable support throughout the ownership period. nigeria.title: ‘Dictator’ Infantino needs psychiatric help, says former FIFA chief Blatter
nigeria.description: Former FIFA boss Sepp Blatter has slammed current chief Gianni Infantino, calling his successor a “dictator” and suggesting he needs psychiatric help, in an interview with Der Spiegel published Wednesday. Blatter, 90, criticised Infantino’s decision to create the FIFA Peace Prize award for US President Donald Trump in the lead-up to this year’s World Cup, hosted in the US, Canada and Mexico. He was also critical of Infantino’s post-World Cup plans to sell off part of the commercial rights of the competition in the future, which was scrapped after a fierce backlash. “FIFA is suffering. It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded,” Blatter told the German magazine. The Peace Prize, he said, was “embarrassing”. “Why would he do something like that?,” Blatter asked. “Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards? That’s madness.” Blatter said it was easy for Infantino to secure support for his own re-election from national football bodies. “‘If you vote for me,’ he tells the national associations, ‘you will get much more money than before.’ “He is a dictator. People in FIFA tell me that no one is allowed to ride in the elevator with him. He is ‘untouchable’.” Speaking of Infantino’s World Cup sale plans, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn’t understand any of this. “I mean, maybe Infantino should be sent to a psychiatric ward one day.” Blatter was also critical of FIFA’s decision to suspend a red card awarded to USA striker Folarin Balogun after Trump intervened ahead of a crucial match at this summer’s World Cup. “The red card. That’s the worst. Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.” – ‘Fulfilling his duties’: FIFA – When contacted for comment by AFP however, FIFA pointed to its previous response to Der Spiegel, which countered Blatter’s statements. FIFA rebutted allegations Infantino had acted inappropriately, saying he “is fulfilling his duties as president through his travels,” while adding: “The suspension imposed on Folarin Balogun following a red card was lifted by independent FIFA judicial bodies.” “Mr. Infantino does indeed use the elevator at FIFA, but does so when other people are present,” FIFA said in the statement. President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations, including accusations he had sought to buy votes for his presidency. nigeria.title: Uganda ruling party rejects plan for son to succeed president
nigeria.description: The leadership of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni’s party has rejected his plan to designate his son, known for boasting of kidnapping and torturing rivals, as his successor, five party sources told AFP on Wednesday. The president’s son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, 52, is currently head of the army, and wields huge and growing influence as his 82-year-old father plays a declining role in governing the east African country after four decades in power. “Muhoozi”, as he is widely known, has vowed to run in the next presidential election scheduled for 2031, but many are unnerved by his flouting of the law, and inflammatory posts on social media, where he frequently boasts of torturing opponents in his “basement”. In recent months, he has had political rivals imprisoned, threatened to behead opposition leader Bobi Wine, and forced the closure of the country’s leading independent media group for several weeks. Although Museveni has ruled with an iron grip since 1986, many within his party, the National Resistance Movement (NRM), have voiced concern at the apparent moves to hand power to his son. In a closed-door meeting of the NRM’s executive committee on Tuesday, convened to determine a successor, a vote on the son’s candidacy had to be abandoned as several of the 28 members spoke against the plan and received loud cheers, according to five people present. Four people had voted in favour of the son, three had voted against, by the time the vote was called off, the sources told AFP. “The combative nature of the (army chief) has created uneasiness among some people. He is fighting and threatening people on social media. Let him start convincing people but not using coercive means to capitulate the population,” said one source. NRM vice-chairman Calvin Echodu told Museveni to retire the son from the army and give him a civilian assignment to get acquainted with the population and prepare himself well for leadership,” said another participant. Echodu also reportedly advised the president that he should stand again in 2031 “as his son is not yet ready,” the source added. The attendees say it was an unprecedented show of defiance against the long-ruling president, who first broached the subject of his succession by presenting a paper to the party grandees in late October, in which he suggested his son had the right credentials for the job. In recent days, Kainerugaba has once again drawn attention with bellicose posts on X, threatening Vice President Jessica Alupo with arrest over claims she was involved in a plot to overthrow the government. Wright, a Professor of Public Health and Community Medicine at the Lagos State University College of Medicine, insisted that women physicians must not limit their contributions to treating patients but should also influence the policies and decisions that determine healthcare delivery. “Not on the sidelines, not behind, not supporting, but we’re at the front,” she declared, stressing that women doctors must be represented in hospital boards, health committees and other decision-making platforms. “We deliver most of the care. She said Nigeria’s maternal mortality ratio of estimated 993 deaths per 100,000 live births was about five times the global average and significantly higher than the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of 70 deaths per 100,000 live births. After we wash them, we have to select and separate them according to their colours, tones, and values.” “I work in two different ways. There’s the assemblage part, where I assemble the footwear. nigeria.title: Bomb threats force evacuation of schools across Italy
nigeria.description: Schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday following a series of bomb threats, which Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described as hoaxes, insisting that there was no concrete danger. The threats, which reportedly affected about 6,000 schools, according to Italian news agency Ansa, citing the Education Ministry, also prompted security concerns in Britain and Ireland, where threatening emails were sent to hundreds of schools. Meloni convened a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs on Wednesday to review the incidents. Although it was unclear how many Italian schools evacuated their students, crowds of schoolchildren were seen outside educational institutions in different parts of the country. Some students said they had to leave their classrooms hurriedly, abandoning their belongings while awaiting police checks. A 19-year-old student at Rome’s Virgilio High School, Sofia De Ponte, told AFP that the school’s principal announced that a bomb threat had been received by email before ordering an evacuation. “The principal came out into the courtyard and told us that an email had come in, a bomb threat, and right after that the building was evacuated,” she said. De Ponte said the police had yet to arrive because “there’s a long waiting list with all the schools”. “We’re still here waiting,” another student, Elena Sicignano, 19, said. At Brera school in Milan, art teacher Violetta Uboldi said some students appeared delighted by the unexpected break from classes. “I think there was a cry of joy because school was over. That was the reaction,” she said. However, a 16-year-old student, Angelica, said the situation initially caused panic because a teacher had told them it was not a drill. Italian media reported that the threatening email was purportedly signed by a person identified as “Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan”. The message claimed that an explosive device had been placed inside a school building and could be detonated remotely. Government Rules Out Immediate Danger The Italian government sought to reassure the public, saying preliminary security checks had not uncovered evidence of an imminent threat. In a Facebook post, Meloni said: “At present, based on the checks carried out, no element has emerged that would suggest there is a concrete danger.” She added that the reports appeared to be part of a strategy designed to cause alarm and concern, adding that investigations were ongoing. Antonello Giannelli, president of the ANP association of Italian school heads, also described the threats as clearly fake. However, he warned that the incident demonstrated how irresponsible actions, amplified by modern communication tools, could cause widespread disruption. “We hope that full light will quickly be shed on the origin of these threats and that those responsible will be identified,” he said. MSCI said on Oct. 15 that the review would carry the final list of current constituents hit by the new screen, with any deletions taking effect at the close of Nov. 30. MSCI’s list of potentially impacted securities, published with the Oct. 15 decision and built on Sept. 30 financial data and Oct. 9 market values, already marks five companies as Deleted: Strategy (MSTR), uranium holder Yellow Cake, Japan’s Metaplanet, Iceland’s Skel Fjárfestingafélag and micro-cap Upexi. Strategy is the only large-cap name in the group and by float-adjusted market value accounts for more than 90% of the five. The company held 850,364 bitcoin as of Nov. 8, acquired at an average price of $75,456 a coin. How the MSCI screen works The rule does not mention bitcoin. MSCI first checks whether a company’s operating assets exceed 50% of total assets. Issuers that fail face five financial ratios, and a company flagged on four or more of them is ineligible for the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes. Buffers limit turnover. A company outside the indexes cannot be added if it fails the screen in either of its two most recent annual filing periods, but a current constituent is removed only if it fails in each of them. MSCI said it may also use the most recent interim filing. That two-filing test is the question hanging over Strategy. It adopted fair-value accounting for its bitcoin at the start of 2025, so its fiscal 2024 statements carried the coins at cost less impairment, and MSCI has not said how it treats that earlier year. A Deleted mark implies MSCI’s draft reading is that Strategy already failed both periods, but it has not published the inputs behind that placement. Strategy has argued that it reports its bitcoin treasury as an operating segment and books related gains and losses in operating expenses. The screen replaces an approach aimed squarely at crypto. MSCI first proposed in late 2025 to exclude companies whose digital assets made up 50% or more of total assets, then dropped that plan in January and opened a broader consultation in August. The new rule also ends the interim measures MSCI placed on those companies in October 2025, including a freeze on share-count increases and a deferral of additions. business.title: Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22 The Bank of Russia said Wednesday that exchanges may start organized trading in cryptocurrencies on Nov. 22, once the central bank has approved their trading rules, a step that lands just ahead of Moscow Exchange’s planned Dec. 1 bitcoin launch. The ordinance, which amends the Bank of Russia’s rules for organized trading, was registered by the Justice Ministry on Nov. 3 and published Wednesday on the regulator’s site. It takes effect 10 days after publication, on Nov. 22. Exchanges will have to register the brokers, trust managers and central counterparties that take part in crypto trades, keep registers of orders and deals, and monitor the activity. They must also calculate a current price, a weighted-average price, a market price and a closing price, and report trading activity to the central bank in the same way they already do for other assets. The regulator was clear about the order of operations. Exchanges may open crypto markets from Nov. 22, it said, “but first they must agree with the regulator on the rules for conducting such trading.” It did not say whether any venue has already cleared that review. Who can buy, and what they can buy A separate ordinance, published Nov. 6 and due to take effect Nov. 17, sets the menu for ordinary buyers. The Bank of Russia approved bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, and said exchanges may admit those assets to public trading from that date. Non-qualified investors can buy through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary may not exceed 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the official exchange rate. Qualified investors can access all cryptoassets with no purchase cap. Both groups still have to pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before they can trade. The list is limited to the most liquid assets that meet the law’s tests for market capitalization, average daily volume and at least five years of pricing history on foreign exchanges. Moscow Exchange still aims for Dec. 1 Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest trading venue, announced on Nov. 2 that it plans to offer bitcoin, ether and USDT trades from Dec. 1, initially as a pilot while participants connect. Trading would run on its existing stock-market systems from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, with the National Clearing Centre clearing the deals and clients able to settle the same day or the next. Bitcoin Magazine reported the Dec. 1 plan last week, including the U.S. sanctions that already cover the exchange and its clearing house. business.title: ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) will open their tokenized stock venue on Nov. 23, the companies said Wednesday, offering more than 70 assets under a temporary SEC exemption even as 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla and Meta, have already objected. The OKX announcement said more than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy (MSTR), as well as 59 exchange-traded funds from Direxion. Strategy will also list its preferred stocks, such as STRC. Access at launch is limited to eligible U.S. customers of OKX Inc. who have activated a CeDeFi Wallet, passed identity checks and completed onboarding with the joint venture, which is called OKXICE and is owned equally by ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc., an OKX affiliate. Trading will run around the clock in the OKX app. “The future of finance is onchain, and we have an opportunity to build it here in America, with the standards, safeguards and ambition that investors expect,” said former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs OKXICE with Trabue Bland. The companies did not say how many of the more than 70 assets will trade on the first day, or how much liquidity the pools will have at the open. The venue is not a registered exchange or broker-dealer and is not approved by the SEC, the announcement said. How the venue will work Trading will run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 and deployed on X Layer, the Ethereum layer-2 network OKX operates. Only approved wallets can trade or add liquidity. Securitize will provide the tokenization infrastructure. Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-for-one by a U.S. share held by a registered broker-dealer, and holders keep the usual shareholder rights, including dividends, voting and corporate actions, the venue said in a Nov. 5 public notice required under the exemption. Customers will hold the tokens in their own wallets. OKXICE will not hold the assets or the private keys. The tokens will be paired with payment stablecoins such as USDC and USDG. The venue does not operate an order book, does not extend credit and does not conduct primary offerings, the notice said. 67 companies have already opted out The same Nov. 5 notice lists 67 issuers that had sent a written objection by that date, among them Apple, Amazon, Tesla, Meta, Netflix, Nvidia, Microsoft, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Costco, Nike and Home Depot. The list has grown from 50 objectors in an Oct. 30 notice. The objections stem from the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued Sept. 17, which lets tokenized securities venues trade blockchain versions of U.S. stocks through automated market makers without registering as exchanges. entertainment.description: Awar Odhiang featured in Vogue wearing a floral printed dress and sculpted oversized rose headpiece. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Remember the model who turned the finale of Matthieu Blazy ‘s first Chanel show into one of the most talked-about runway moments of 2025? That was Awar Odhiang, and she has another major reason to celebrate. The South Sudanese-Canadian model has been named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026. The 25-year-old will receive the honour at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 30 November. Born in a refugee camp in Ethiopia and raised in Canada, Awar’s journey to the international fashion scene has taken her from being discovered in Alberta to walking some of the world’s biggest runways. She is now represented by major modelling agencies across London, Milan, Paris and New York. Awar Odhiang walking the red carpet at the 2026 Met Gala in New York City. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her runway résumé includes shows for Prada, Versace, Miu Miu, Saint Laurent and Jacquemus, but it was her appearance at Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2026 show in October 2025 that introduced her to an even wider audience. Closing Matthieu Blazy’s first collection for the fashion house, Awar wore the show’s bridal look, featuring an oversized white shirt and a voluminous, colourful feathered skirt. But it was what happened at the finale that captured everyone’s attention. As the models gathered for their final walk, Awar broke formation, smiling, clapping and twirling in her skirt. When Blazy appeared, she ran towards him and embraced him. The spontaneous moment quickly went viral, with fashion fans celebrating the joy she brought to the runway. It was also a historic appearance: Awar became only the third Black woman to close a Chanel show in the house’s 115-year history, after Alek Wek and Adut Akech. Model of the Year 2026 winner Awar Odhiang backstage at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Since then, her career has continued to gather pace. Awar has appeared on eight international magazine covers this year and fronted campaigns for Chanel, Chloé, Louis Vuitton, Saint Laurent, Loro Piana and H&M. She has also used her growing platform to speak up for greater representation and inclusion of Black models in the luxury fashion industry. Awar Odhiang in Daniel Roseberry’s Schiaparelli Spring 2026 Haute Couture collection in Paris. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her Model of the Year recognition celebrates a remarkable year of runway, editorial and campaign work, as well as the influence she continues to have beyond the catwalk. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. sports.description: Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski reacts after a three-point basket against the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of an NBA Cup basketball game, Saturday, Oct. 30, 2026, in San Francisco. At some point, Podziemski posed a simple if heavy question: What about Steph? Stephen Curry counts as a model of efficient movement and basketball creativity. And the trainer, Dustin VanLieu, knew exactly how to help Podziemski gain deeper insight from his decorated Golden State Warriors teammate – magically make Curry left-handed. VanLieu flipped videos of Curry – let's pause here for a nod to the power of digital editing tools – to turn No. 30 into a mirrored version of himself. That allowed Podziemski, who is lefty, to study the footwork, ball-handling and shot creation of a left-handed Steph Curry. The images are striking, as Curry scurries around the court like a familiar if semi-fictional character. He dribbles around bewildered opponents, as usual – even dropping Luka Doncic to the hardwood, on what looks like the opposite end of the court than the real-life moment Oct. 30 – but the sight of Curry launching long-range shots with his left hand is strangely captivating. Curry wasn't aware of Podziemski's uncommon preparation until the Chronicle showed him a video after Saturday night's overtime victory over Orlando. sports.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
sports.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. sports.title: David Warner starts fresh Sandpapergate row after Graeme Hick rejects Khawaja's dressing-room claims
sports.description: The infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight following fresh revelations by Usman Khawaja, triggering a war of words between former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick and David Warner. While Hick has strongly rejected Khawaja's claims that the entire Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper, Warner has hit back at the former coach, questioning his appointment and bringing Michael Di Venuto into the debate. What did Graeme Hick say about Khawaja's claims? Hick, who was part of Australia's coaching staff during the 2018 South Africa tour, described Khawaja's allegations as "absolutely false". He maintained that he had no knowledge of any discussions about using sandpaper and only became aware of the incident after seeing the footage on the big screen in Cape Town. Khawaja had claimed that the entire dressing room was aware of the ball-tampering, suggesting that responsibility for the incident went beyond the three players who were eventually punished. Warner responded by taking aim at Hick's appointment as Australia's batting coach, bringing former assistant coach Michael Di Venuto into the discussion. In response to an X post on the interview, Warner wrote: "Let's get the facts straight. Graeme Hick was only appointed because Cricket Australia was unwilling to pay Michael Di Venuto what he deserved. As players, we valued Michael so highly that we even offered to contribute from our own salaries to retain him. These discussions were taking place during the New Zealand tour. That alone speaks volumes about how highly we regarded him and how determined we were to keep him involved. Adds to why Graeme has spoken!!" — davidwarner31 (@davidwarner31) Why has the 2018 Sandpapergate controversy resurfaced? The latest exchange follows the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr, in which the Australia batter revisited the events of the 2018 South Africa tour. His account has reopened questions about how much the dressing room knew about the ball-tampering incident and whether the original investigation captured the full extent of what happened. The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball using a piece of sandpaper. The incident became known as Sandpapergate and led to major sanctions against the players involved. Warner and then Australia captain Steve Smith were handed one-year suspensions by Cricket Australia, while Bancroft received a nine-month ban. The episode also led to widespread criticism of Australian cricket and prompted questions about the team's culture and leadership.

He made his first major championship start at Aronimink a few months later. Not discouraged from the missed cut at the PGA Championship, the 32-year-old Smotherman won for the first time in his 100th start on Tour at the Bank of Utah Championship. He didn't let the time between career win No. 1 and No. 2 last very long. Three weeks later in Bermuda, Smotherman stood in the winner’s circle again after ousting Seamus Power in a two-man playoff after weather cut the tournament short to 54 holes. With all that, his playing status secured through 2029. And now, one more mountain to climb: Finish inside the top 50 of the Official World Golf Ranking. If he clinches that before the end of the season, the No. 51-ranked Smotherman will get his first-ever invite to Augusta National. There's some risk involved — two missed cuts could theoretically send him down, outside the top 60 in the FedExCup fall points and lose his spot in the first two signature events of 2027. It's a bet Smotherman is willing to take considering the possible reward. "Do our best to put up good weeks and earn some more World Ranking points and cap off the fall hopefully on a high note," he said at his press conference at this week’s Austin Championship when asked about his plan for the next couple of weeks. "Can't take away what we did," Smotherman added. "If we miss two cuts coming up, still doing a lot well and it was the best decision I think to go give it a run. The world ranking points system, I don't understand it perfectly, that's for my team to tell me what's going on. I'm just going to go play golf." Austin Championship - Rd 1 The Austin Championship tees off at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa in Austin, Texas. Smotherman, who turned pro in 2016 and played in Latin America the following year, credited the experience from traveling the world for helping him land where he is ahead of the season-finale tournament in Georgia next week. "I feel like my good's been good enough to have a chance to win out here for a long time," the back-to-back winner said. "I made a bunch of cuts, I've had stretches of a lot of missed cuts, I feel like I've done everything in between," he added. "So to cap off wins now is a different feeling kind of getting that under my belt." This week the SMU grad will be playing in front of friends and family in Austin, not too far from where he lives in Dallas. "These last two weeks everybody's kind of questioning, oh, 'Why are you playing, what have you got going on?' sports.title: Jets insider savagely dunks on Aaron Glenn’s ‘on the cusp’ claim after quiet trade deadline
sports.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Jets insider savagely dunks on Aaron Glenn’s ‘on the cusp’ claim after quiet trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets were not buyers at the NFL trade deadline this year. New York was active, but only to ship off Andre Cisco to Detroit . The Jets do not look like a playoff team this year, but should they have tried harder to add talent at the trade deadline? Jets head coach Aaron Glenn explained why the team did not make any moves at the deadline this year. “Listen, we’re not going to hide from the fact that we’re 2-7. We own that, but, man, we’re still working our asses off to make sure we fix that. We feel like we like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that,” Glenn said on Wednesday, per ESPN’s Rich Cimini. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Glenn also explained why he thinks New York is “on the cusp” despite their terrible record. “When you look at the seven losses, and this is just the facts — five of the teams (are) playoff-caliber teams. I think five of them were one-score games. I think two (of the losses were) three points, one five-point and two seven points.” However, Cimini was quick to note that New York has played the 23rd hardest schedule this season, per ESPN analytics. Even if the Jets are playing their opponents closely, they’re still losing games. It is certainly fair to point out that the Jets are still a long way from being a contender. But that could all change during the 2027 offseason. The Jets will have three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. If everything breaks their way, New York could even have three picks in the top 10. Not only could they find a franchise quarterback, but they could also add a few blue-chip players as well. The future is bright for the Jets, but it is still frustrating to see them take a passive approach to the trade deadline. Regardless, next up for New York is a Week 10 home game against Buffalo. sports.title: Oregon's Lanning delivers KO response to Michigan's Whittingham
sports.description: Two days after Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said that Oregon coach Dan Lanning has “$50-plus million” to build a football team, Lanning responded with a dig. Lanning 1, Whittingham 0. More: 'Regression' led to Jason Beck's firing as Michigan offensive coordinator More: Should Kyle Whittingham get another season to turn things around at UM? | Take our poll The coaches will face each other on Saturday, Nov. 14, when Michigan plays at Oregon’s Autzen Stadium. Michigan is 5-4, 2-4 Big Ten, while Oregon is 6-3, 4-2. “Outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach,” Whittingham said Monday, Nov. 9, on the “Inside Michigan Football” radio show, referring to Lanning. “Tireless recruiter. He really does a great job recruiting. It doesn’t hurt that you have $50-plus million at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. That’s not his fault. That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. “NIL is really the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much. It used to be the facilities you had, the tradition, all these other things. And now it’s, ‘Well, this is all great. But these guys have got 100 grand more for me.’ So, that’s a little bit of a factor to say the least. Not to take anything away from Dan because he is an outstanding recruiter.” Michigan reportedly has a budget of $40 million for its roster. Lanning, at his news conference on Wednesday, Nov. 11, was asked about Whittingham’s comments regarding Oregon’s budget. "Man, I've got nothing to say to Coach Whitt other than I think he's an unbelievable coach," Lanning told reporters. “And I get it — they're spending more money on the coaches they're letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players, but I know they've signed a couple guys that we weren't able to compete with what they decided to do and maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player, I don't know. But Coach Whittingham is an unbelievable coach. He's a Hall of Fame coach. I've got nothing but respect for him." Lanning’s not-so-subtle reference was to Whittingham’s firing of offensive coordinator Jason Beck last Sunday, Nov. 8, after nine games. Michigan owes Beck nearly $10 million after being fired in the first-year of a three-year contract. Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor delivered an apology on behalf of Duke Tobin on Wednesday after the team’s proposed trade for Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie fell through. The Bengals had agreed to acquire Ebiketie for a 2027 sixth-round pick before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The Bengals withdrew after determining the move would also cost a projected third-round compensatory pick. Speaking to reporters in Cincinnati, Taylor said Tobin wanted the organization to accept responsibility , according to ESPN’s Ben Baby. Because Ebiketie signed as a compensatory free agent during the offseason, acquiring him would have affected Cincinnati’s compensatory-pick formula. That changed the price beyond the sixth-round selection included in the initial agreement, leaving Ebiketie in Philadelphia. Cincinnati sought help after placing rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell on injured reserve November 3 with a right wrist injury. The second-round pick from Texas A&M has not been ruled out for the season. The Bengals enter Sunday night’s home matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers at 6-2, with the proposed addition off the table and Howell still on injured reserve. sports.title: Yaxel Lendeborg could make strange history in the Rookie of the Year vote this season
sports.description: Not many had high hopes for the Golden State Warriors this season, not with Jimmy Butler (and Moses Moody ) set to miss so much time as they recover from their respective injuries. And yet the team currently sits at 8-3, sixth overall in the West, and the deeper numbers - Golden State ranks No. 2 in offensive efficiency in 2026-27 and No. 11 in defensive efficiency - also support their hot start. On the other hand, this season, the Warriors are currently hitting 43.6 percent of their threes that NBA.com labels as wide open, the second-best mark in the league, so it's fair to wonder about the sustainability of that number. We think Stephen Curry will continue hitting his threes at a high clip, obviously, but will De'Anthony Melton , Will Richard , Al Horford and Brandin Podziemski keep shooting between 42.9 and 40.3 percent from three? That remains to be seen. There's another player on Golden State's roster currently scorching hot from three, and that's rookie phenom Yaxel Lendeborg . Lendeborg has been nothing short of a revelation for the Warriors, a breath of fresh air in a skilled 6-foot-9 package who can score from all three levels, rebound, create and defend, and who is looking like an absolute steal for Golden State, who got him with the 11th pick in the most recent draft. Absolutely no one expected Lendeborg to be as good as he is right away in the Association, as evidenced by the fact that his own college head coach at Michigan, Dusty May , didn't force the current team he's coaching, the Dallas Mavericks, to draft him with the team's ninth pick. And yet, here we are, with Lendeborg playing like an All-Star in his first season and helping carry the Warriors to an impressive start. The former Michigan standout is averaging 21.4 points, 7.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.0 steals per game on 52.3 percent shooting from the floor and 44.3 percent shooting from three so far this season. He ranks Top 16 in our Global Rating metric and Top 30 in BPM league-wide. The only other rookies to put up a 21/7/4 stat line in their inaugural campaigns? Four Hall of Famers ( Kareem Abdul-Jabbar , Oscar Robertson , Larry Bird and Elgin Baylor ), one future Hall of Famer ( Luka Doncic ) and a four-time All-Star ( Sidney Wicks ). Solid company there for the San Juan native. sports.description: Three days after the Detroit Red Wings sent him down , Nate Danielson made the most of his first game back in the AHL. The 22-year-old center recorded three assists in the Grand Rapids Griffins’ 6-3 win over the Rockford IceHogs on Wednesday morning, his first game of the season with Grand Rapids. sports.title: Reds offseason plans take hit with Emilio Pagán signing with Detroit
sports.description: LAS VEGAS – The Cincinnati Reds ' impossible-dream offseason just got a lot tougher with the Detroit Tigers ' $11.5 million signing of free agent Reds closer Emilio Pagán . The one-year agreement, which comes three weeks before an anticipated MLB labor lockout, also includes a bonus package. Until the deal was struck, the Reds were keeping in touch with Pagán for a possible return since declining a $10 million option for 2027 less than two weeks ago. Manager Terry Francona said as recently as Nov. 6 during a radio interview that he held out hope that Pagán would return. Pagán, 35, converted all 19 save chances with a 1.88 ERA after returning from a severe hamstring injury for the final three months of the season. He became the Reds' closer in April 2025 and earned a career-high 32 saves with a 2.88 ERA on the way to the playoffs that year. “I loved having him. He was great,” team president Nick Krall said of the veteran who was valued almost as much for his clubhouse influence as his high-level performance on the mound. “He’s been really good for us the last three, four years.” One of the reasons a return seemed plausible when Pagán opted out of his Reds contract was that he returned as a free agent a year ago after his original two-year, $16 million deal with the Reds expired. Both sides said the door was open to return and continued a dialogue. The Reds went from that playoff berth in 2025 to last place this year, their hitters striking out more and scoring less than anyone else in the league, their pitchers walking more than anyone else and their fielding ranking among the worst in the majors. Now they have to add a closer to a laundry list of needs to fill to have any semblance of a chance to return to the playoffs – which they continue to say is their goal. Krall looks like he's working without a net in that effort. He's definitely working without a payroll budget, which he said has not been determined as he spoke in Las Vegas this week during MLB's annual GM meetings. So where does all of that put the Reds’ thinking when it comes to the enormous ninth-inning hole in their pitching staff? Try to fill it specifically with an acquisition during an uncertain winter? Throw a bunch of arms into a spring competition and see where it lands? “Obviously you’d love to build the bullpen from the back forward,” Krall said. “But it’s something we’re just going to work through this offseason, and we’ll do the best we can.” This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Reds offseason plans take hit with Emilio Pagán signing with Detroit

technology.title: US bit barn boom sees energy needs grow 10x as fast as grid capacity
technology.description: Datacenter power consumption in the US is growing roughly ten times faster than grid capacity, meaning facilities may soon need to find a large chunk of their own electricity from other sources. Surging demand for AI infrastructure is driving a wave of new server farms across America, but it is exposing long-term underinvestment in the grid networks required to deliver power where it's needed. Insurance broker Howden calculates that datacenters would need to source up to 58 percent of their power off the grid by 2030 just to keep their share of grid capacity from growing. Gartner warned in June that the energy consumed by AI datacenters is on track to grow 26 percent this year, and grid supply may be unable to keep pace with demand by the end of this decade. Howden's analysis of data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and S&P Global found that since the year 2000, power being fed to data campuses has risen 19 percent a year on average, while the electricity grid expanded capacity by just 2 percent per annum over the same period. Datacenters' share of US grid capacity was circa five percent in 2025, up from 0.1 percent in 2000 – a 50-fold increase. Management consultancy Bain & Company issued a report two years ago warning that energy companies must switch gear and invest in building out grid capacity faster , as energy draw by server farms is expected to more than double by 2030. This doesn't mean that datacenters are in danger of eating all of America's electricity, at least not in the immediate future. The graph makes it appear that the two lines are about to cross, but the chart uses different scales: 1,400 gigawatts on the left axis for grid capacity, versus just 80 on the right for datacenters. Keeping datacenters at five percent of grid capacity requires 110 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity by 2030, Howden estimates – an expansion it considers unlikely. Instead, it expects a combination of greater reliance on the grid, slower development at power-constrained sites, and alternative supplies. For the largest, most power-constrained projects, Howden warns that grid delays of two to six years could mean $800 million to $2.4 billion in forgone revenue. "Power availability is becoming one of the defining challenges of the datacenter boom," says Howden head of Natural Resources Stuart Adam. "As demand for AI infrastructure accelerates, developers are increasingly looking beyond traditional grid connections to secure the electricity they need." Howden's business is insurance, and so Adam also notes that on-site generation introduces new operational and financial exposures, as operators take greater responsibility for their power infrastructure. ®

technology.title: Scientists check their work and confirm it with update on iconic black hole image
technology.description: The image of the red ring around the black hole M87, produced by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) array, made front-page news around the world in 2019. There was one problem: there was a slim chance the depiction might be wrong. This week, a small team of four Australian researchers have published their work confirming the result based on a new machine learning algorithm using the same base data. The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image came from hundreds of scientists working together to capture the first direct view of a black hole's shadow. The measurements were taken at eight telescopes around the world, at locations including Chile, the US, and Antarctica. Reconstructing the image from the data so geographically distant meant instrument and environment errors could influence the accuracy of the resulting image. Potentially, alternative analyses of the data could have reconstructed an image without the iconic ring shape. Samuel Lai – a postdoctoral fellow at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) in Western Australia – and his team created an independent imaging algorithm to process the historic dataset to validate the result. The new approach used closed triplets (using three telescopes for error correction) rather than station pairs in an effort to reduce error. To the relief of the EHT team, the new image recreated the iconic ring-like image seen in the original, according to a paper published in Nature today . In a prepared statement, Lai said taking pictures of black holes was not easy. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the Moon," he said. He explained that when his team applied new advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to the original Event Horizon Telescope dataset, they found a black hole almost identical in size and shape to the historic EHT image. "Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data. This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process," he said. Event Horizon Telescope director Laurent Loinard welcomed the new study. "It is extremely gratifying to see that an elegant, entirely independent method recovers the ring structure of M87 across several years, in excellent agreement with the EHT Collaboration's published results," he said. ®

science.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
science.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space. Catching one takes luck, as a telescope has to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right moment. That changed with CHIME (the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) in British Columbia. With a very wide field of view and a supercomputer to process its data, CHIME more than quadrupled the number of known FRBs in its first year of operation alone. Between 2018 and 2023, CHIME recorded 4,539 bursts from 3,641 sources. As pulses of radio waves, our eyes haven't evolved to see FRBs, nor can we hear them as they aren't sound waves. Well, not until now. "Artist and composer Andrew Melchior turned all of the CHIME bursts into sound for "The Logos," an installation that has played daily at Oulu Cathedral in Finland since early April and is scheduled to run through the end of the year. Melchior and Kiyoshi Masui, an associate professor of physics at MIT, "sonified" the bursts, translating data into acoustics so that human ears can hear them. The structure of each real signal is mapped to varying musical pitches and played through 12 loudspeakers spread throughout the cathedral. The result is a range of tones, with distant FRBs humming, rumbling, popping, and whistling. The signals are old by any human measure. According to a description on Melchior's website , the youngest in the work are about 50 million years old, and the oldest are about 8 to 9 billion years old. Saxton, NRAO/AUI/NSF)) Physics also plays a role in what is heard. Each burst arrives with its high frequencies first and sweeps downward, stretched by its journey through intergalactic gas, "and you can hear that dispersion as it falls from the dome," Melchior told Space.com by email. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA launches Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day. The astronauts returned to Earth after four days in space. Both Aldrin and Lovell went on to join the Apollo program . Aldrin became the second person to walk on the moon during Apollo 11 , and Lovell became the commander of Apollo 13 . The Gemini 12 astronauts James Lovell and Edwin Aldrin lifted off aboard a Titan launch vehicle from the Kennedy Space Center on November 11, 1966, an hour and a half after their Agena target vehicle was orbited by an Atlas rocket. (Image credit: NASA/MSFC) Why it mattered Gemini 12 may have closed out NASA's Gemini program of two-person space missions, but it established the mission also established the fundamentals of spacewalking that Apollo astronauts would use when they walked on the moon. It's fitting that Aldrin was the primary spacewalker of the mission. A rookie astronaut (and the first to earn a Ph.D.), Aldrin set a precedent by training for his spacewalk in a neutral buoyancy pool in Maryland to better simulate working in weightlessness. Then he did it again as the second person to walk on the moon on Apollo 11. "This approach became so successful, underwater training has become the primary spacewalk training method used by the United State, Russia and China," NASA officials said in a mission overview . "Today, NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory in Houston is large enough to include mockups of major sections of the International Space Station . science.title: Blood-thinning drug limits cartilage damage and relieves osteoarthritis pain
science.description: Coloured X-ray of osteoarthritis of the knee ALAIN POL/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY A drug that prevents blood clots reduced pain and improved mobility in mice and monkeys with knee osteoarthritis. The approach seems to partly work by reducing inflammatory signals that degrade cartilage. Osteoarthritis is caused by the wear and tear of cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, leading to inflammation, pain and stiffness. It affects more than 500 million people worldwide. Painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs can relieve symptoms, but no approved drugs halt or slow worsening of the disease. “We have nothing to offer our patients apart from suggesting weight loss, or offering drugs that provide pain relief,” says Tonia Vincent at the University of Oxford, who wasn’t involved in the study. Advertisement Read more The best non-drug therapies to relieve the pain of knee osteoarthritis It is widely thought that inflammatory molecules called TNF-alpha and IL-1-beta drive inflammation that worsens osteoarthritis. This has led to clinical trials testing drugs that target either of these molecules. But these have been unsuccessful, potentially because these molecules compensate for each other when one is blocked, according to Chuan-Ju Liu at Yale University and his colleagues. To explore whether targeting both molecules may be more effective, the researchers surgically removed part of the cartilage in the left knee joints of eight monkeys to mimic wear and tear that triggers osteoarthritis. A month later, four of the monkeys took a daily dose of a drug called dabigatran, mixed into their food. Dabigatran is commonly used to prevent blood clots in people at increased risk of strokes, but has also been shown to block inflammatory signals via both TNF-alpha and IL-1-beta. The remaining monkeys ate their usual food as a control. This suggests that the drug reduced cartilage damage, slowing the progression of osteoarthritis, says Liu. Monkeys on dabigratan also had a roughly 15 per cent greater range of motion in their left knee than the control monkeys. “Monkeys receiving dabigatran showed a more natural walking pattern and a greater range of knee movement,” says Liu. “These improvements are consistent with reduced joint stiffness and discomfort.” In further experiments, the team confirmed their findings in mice with surgically-induced knee osteoarthritis, which also revealed that dabigratan reduced inflammation in the knee by about 60 per cent.
